articles.title: La Federación y la Liga Saudí condenan los lamentables cánticos contra Diogo Jota
articles.standfirst: Ocurrió durante el partido entre Al-Taawoun y Al-Hilal
articles.summary: Ocurrió durante el partido entre Al-Taawoun y Al-Hilal
articles.body: Tanto la Federación Saudí de Fútbol como la Liga Profesional Saudí han condeado públicamente los cánticos de la afición de Al Taawoun contra la memoria del tristemente fallecido Diogo Jota. Los insultos iban contra Rúben Neves, amigo íntimo de Jota, en el partido que enfrentaba a Al Taawoun con Al Hilal, equipo en el que juega el internacional portugués. "La Federación Saudí de Fútbol (SAFF) y la Liga Profesional Saudí (SPL) condenan la conducta inaceptable de algunos aficionados presentes durante el partido de la Liga Saudí Roshn entre Al Taawoun y Al Hilal, que es incompatible con los valores del fútbol saudí y los principios de la deportividad. La SAFF y la SPL subrayan que explotar tragedias personales con fines de abuso o provocación es un comportamiento inaceptable que no tiene cabida en el fútbol saudí. SAFF confirma que los comités pertinentes han identificado la conducta en cuestión y tomarán las medidas necesarias de conformidad con las normas y procedimientos aplicables. El resultado se anunciará una vez concluido el proceso correspondiente", es el comunicado de ambos organismos saudíes. Rúben Neves, que salió visiblemente enfadado tras lo ocurrido, compareció en zona mixta: "Solo espero que no se vayan a rezar después de lo que hicieron". En las últimas horas, también Cristiano Ronaldo denunció dichos cánticos y condenó "tales excesos, especialmente cuando van dirigidos a los jugadores o a sus familias, o buscan atacarlos personalmente". El de Madeira anunció que había presentado una queja formal ante la Federación para "proteger los derechos del club y de sus jugadores".

articles.title: Aberdeen may face disciplinary action over supporter behaviour at Kilmarnock
articles.summary: Aberdeen could face disciplinary action after some supporters invaded the Rugby Park pitch following their cup win over Kilmarnock.
articles.body:
Aberdeen could face disciplinary action after some supporters invaded the Rugby Park pitch following their Premier Sports Cup win over Kilmarnock on Saturday.

Jack Milne scored the winning penalty to seal a 3-1 shootout victory after the sides were tied 1-1 at the end of extra-time, and the Dons will face Rangers in next month's semi-final at Hampden Park.

Tournament organisers, the Scottish Professional Football League, will investigate the post-match episode in East Ayrshire and also ask the Pittodrie club for an explanation into the use of pyrotechnics during the quarter-final.

The SPFL cut Rangers and Celtic's allocation for Hampden after the widespread use of flares disrupted League Cup semi-finals last season.

And the SPFL and Scottish FA are looking into getting tough on unacceptable conduct in Scottish football.

Both Old Firm clubs have been ordered to play their next home matches in the Scottish Cup behind closed doors following trouble during and after a quarter-final tie at Ibrox in March.

articles.title: Arsenal want explanation over penalty awarded to Sunderland
articles.summary: Arsenal will seek an explanation from Pro Ref for the penalty awarded against them in their Premier League win at Sunderland. Manager Mikel Arteta described...
articles.body:
Arsenal will seek an explanation from Pro Ref for the penalty awarded against them in their Premier League win at Sunderland .

Manager Mikel Arteta described referee John Brooks' decision to penalize Ezri Konsa for an adjudged foul on Dan Ballard , with VAR not intervening, as "unacceptable".

The Press Association understands that the Premier League champions will contact refereeing body Pro Ref for clarity on the second-half flashpoint.

The spot-kick was taken by Enzo Le Fee and brilliantly saved by David Raya , before Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka scored in a 2-0 win to retain Arsenal's 100 per cent start to the season.

However, Arteta was furious with the decision which he said could have cost his side a victory at the Stadium of Light.

"It is not acceptable," he said. "I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they'd think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"At this level with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

Arsenal will take on Ipswich at Portman Road in the League Cup on Wednesday before they head to Brighton in the league this weekend as they bid to make it five wins from five.

articles.title: Ligue 1 Review | Brest remember King Eric on night of tributes
articles.summary: There wasn’t a dry eye in the stands at the Stade Francis-Le Blé before kickoff on Sunday evening as Stade Brestois and Paris Saint-Germain came together to...
articles.body:
There wasn't a dry eye in the stands at the Stade Francis-Le Blé before kickoff on Sunday evening as Stade Brestois and Paris Saint-Germain came together to pay tribute to the memory of the late Éric Roy.

The Brest coach passed away in June at the age of 58 following a battle with pancreatic cancer. King Eric, as he had come to be known during his three years in charge of Les Pirates , left an indelible mark on the club and city as a whole.

His daughter spoke to the stadium before the match: " We wanted to thank the team, the Brest University Hospital for supporting Dad during his illness, thank the fans – thank you for your words, thank you for your songs, for your messages. There was so much love here . It's absolutely incredible.

" We are so happy that he was able to experience this before he passed away. Football is about love, passion, and connection. That's what he passed on to you, and he will continue to spread it from where he is, through you, through us. Thank you, long live Brest !" She said.

Connection felt like the word to pick up on in a beautiful statement, because it has been the theme underpinning Brest since Roy's tragic death. From the internal appointment of Julien Lachuer as the head coach, an assistant under Roy, there's a feeling of legacy to this team.

There's the sense that Brest are building on and honouring the foundations left by their former King rather than uprooting and starting anew. And this continuity has contributed to a promising start to the campaign, where Les Pirates could be a little disappointed to have only taken five points from four games.

As Luis Enrique said after watching his PSG side come away with a narrow 1-0 win courtesy of Ferran Torres ' fifth-minute strike, " It's incredible that we won this game when it was the worst of the four we've played ." According to Opta , Brest should be top of the Ligue 1 table on expected points.

It was a performance against PSG to make their former head coach proud. As the Brest midfielder Hugo Magnetti explained in the mixed zone after the game, " That was our goal, and coach Lachuer made that clear in his pre-match speech. He really emphasised the point; his words resonated deeply with everyone. "

Magnetti continued, " We truly wanted to pay tribute to this great man, to give everything for him. He would have been proud of us, but he would have also given us a bit of a talking-to because we missed some big chances ."

For a club in mourning, there might have been a fear at the start of the season that the football would have come back too soon; the emotion would be too raw. Instead, that rawness has brought the club together, uniting each aspect more deeply. And on a night of tributes, it was on the pitch that a fitting one was left for King Roy.

Lost in the emotion of the night was the fact that it was PSG's first win of the Ligue 1 season. Whether it will be the turning point that the club have been searching for domestically remains to be seen. Up next is Le Classique.

articles.title: Cuatro goleadores empatados en el liderato del Pichichi
articles.standfirst: Todos ellos llevan seis goles en cinco jornadas
articles.summary: Todos ellos llevan seis goles en cinco jornadas
articles.body: Es raro que se dé estas coincidencias en el comienzo del campeonato, sobre todo en el ámbito goleador, donde todo fluctúa más, pero que hasta cuatro futbolistas lleguen a la cifra de seis goles en cinco jornadas es, cuando menos, contrario a todo tipo de lógica estadística. Raphina, Camello, Lamine y Mbappé son los cuatro atacantes que coronan la cima anotadora de este comienzo de curso. Destaca sobre todo el papel del delantero rayista, que con el tanto anotado el pasado sábado en el Bernabéu está cosechando su mejor arranque desde que llegó a la élite del fútbol español. En cuanto a los otros tres goleadores, huelga decir que no es raro verles en posiciones tan avanzadas, sin embargo es altamente reseñable que el rodillo azulgrana de cara a la portería contraria se debe en gran medida en el tándem que integran Raphinha y Lamine. En lo que al resto de goleadores se refiere destaca, cómo no, Aubameyang, quien con su cinco de cinco está soprendiendo a propios y extraños en cada partido que disputa. El apartado de la portería (El Zamora) está liderado por Agirrezabala, con un total de 23 puntos; seguido de Dmitrovic (Espanyol), Herrero (Málaga), Remiro (Real Sociedad) y Ryan (Levante). En LaLiga Hypermotion hay tablas también, siendo Asprilla el atacante y Enric Gallego (Tenerife) quienes ocupan el puesto más alto en el Pichichi de la División de Plata con cuatro tantos. A continuación sigue Adri Fuentes (Mallorca), con tres dianas, así como Nicholas Gioacchini (Sabadell) En cuanto a los líderes bajo palos, entre los mejores se colocan Matthys, del Castellón; Arnay Tenas (Mallorca); Dani Martín (Tenerife) y Yáñez (Sporting).

articles.title: Daniel Maldini: Son of Italy and AC Milan legend Paolo has drivers license suspended after car crash
articles.summary: Italy international Daniel Maldini has his driving licence suspended following a car crash in Milan.
articles.body:
Italy international Daniel Maldini has had his driving licence suspended after he was found to be over the legal alcohol limit following a car crash in Milan.

Maldini, son of Italy and AC Milan legend Paolo and grandson of the similarly feted Cesare, was one among six people to suffer minor injuries after his Porsche Carrera 4 collided with another vehicle in the early hours of Sunday.

The attacking midfielder had scored the winning goal for Cagliari in a 2-1 win against his parent club Atalanta in Serie A just hours before the accident.

Milan city police confirmed to BBC Sport that there had been a road traffic accident involving the 24-year-old footballer.

It said: "Mr Maldini was administered a breathalyser test at the scene" and his "driving license was confiscated following a positive result".

He was taken to hospital for precautionary checks before being released.

According to reports, an initial breath test carried out by the police at the scene of the accident recorded a blood alcohol level of 0.91 grams per litre, while a second reading registered 0.89 g/l - both higher than Italy's legal limit of 0.5 g/l.

In a statement, Cagliari said Maldini had "undergone toxicological screening following recent media reports" and that "all tests returned negative results".

The club added Maldini will join the squad for training on Monday to prepare for the team's forthcoming fixtures.

Maldini became became the third generation of his family to play for Italy when he made his debut against Israel in a Nations League fixture in 2024.

He has made six appearances for his country, with the latest coming in September 2025.

articles.title: Hakimi mantiene en vilo al PSG para 'Le Classique'
articles.standfirst: El conjunto parisino emitió un primer veredicto acerca de la lesión sufrida por el internacional marroquí en el duelo frente al Brest
articles.summary: El conjunto parisino emitió un primer veredicto acerca de la lesión sufrida por el internacional marroquí en el duelo frente al Brest
articles.body: Problemas para el PSG y Luis Enrique. Achraf Hakimi, tal y como informó el club en un comunicado emitido en sus redes sociales, sufrió una lesión muscular contra el Brest y su participación en 'Le Classique' ante el Olympique de Marsella este mismo fin de semana está prácticamente descartada. El PSG no informó acerca del alcance de la lesión. Sin embargo, sí emitió un primer veredicto en el que reflejó que existe un problema muscular. "Achraf Hakimi sufrió una leve distensión en el muslo derecho contra el Brest y recibirá tratamiento durante los próximos dos días. Se proporcionará más información al final de este período", podía leerse en la nota emitida por el club. La lesión tuvo lugar a poco más de cinco minutos de finalizar la primera parte en el Stade Francis-Le Blé. Rápidamente, se llevó la mano a la pierna derecha y no mostró ninguna intención de volver al terreno de juego para probarse hasta el descanso. Luis Enrique, que tampoco quiso correr riesgo alguno, lo sustituyó por Fabián Ruiz. Fue Zaïre-Emery quien se ubicó como lateral derecho. Una situación que, ni mucho menos, le cogió por sorpresa al joven internacional francés. Durante gran parte de la temporada pasada tuvo que desempeñarse en dicha demarcación a raíz de la lesión que sufrió el propio Hakimi contra el Bayern mediada la temporada. También, cabe la posibilidad de que Luis Enrique comience a meter en dinámica a David Boly (2009). "No sé el nivel de su lesión. Veremos con las pruebas médicas. No hay nada importante, pero está lesionado", dio a conocer 'Lucho' después del encuentro. "Espero que la lesión no sea grave, es difícil determinarlo. Se someterá a un examen médico mañana", recalcó el técnico asturiano. A falta de confirmación oficial, la presencia del marroquí frente al OM está prácticamente descartada. La buena noticia, por verlo de algún modo, es que el PSG tiene toda la semana limpia antes de afrontar un primer parón que, en esta ocasión, se alargará hasta tres semanas. Achraf, por tanto, tendrá tiempo para recuperarse con la vista puesta en el duelo ante el Manchester City el próximo 14 de octubre.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Stock Report: Ashton Jeanty, Colston Loveland among notable risers, fallers in Week 1
articles.summary: Here are the players who helped and hurt their stock after Week 1 of fantasy football.
articles.body:
As I write this on Sunday night, all but one Week 1 game is comfortably in the books, and as is always the case on opening weekend, we encountered a slew of surprises. Some promising, others concerning and many that may have affected our outlook on a player or an offense. We're all doing our best not to overreact to one Sunday (and one Wednesday and one Thursday), but some of these shifting perspectives are bound to have permanent ramifications.

With that in mind, I've compiled the (first) full weekly fantasy football stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 2.

Ankle sprain, schmankle schprain (sorry, editors). Ashton Jeanty looked incredible on Sunday and had absolutely no limitations on his workload. He handled 23 carries and had six catches, totaling 147 yards while scoring twice through the air. He totaled 74 rushing yards after contact and scored both of his receiving touchdowns from the 13-yard line. Translation? The second-year RB's upside is arguably somewhere in the Christian McCaffrey stratosphere. The one caveat to all of this, of course, is that he did it against the Miami Dolphins . We'll see whether things change in Week 2 against the Chargers. But for now, Jeanty looks fully healthy and completely dominant, and anyone who got him at the "ankle sprain discount" is doing cartwheels.

At just 61% rostered on Yahoo, Jalen Coker was closer to being a waiver-wire player than a fantasy stud. Not anymore. The third-year wideout led the Panthers with nine targets, eight catches, 138 receiving yards and two touchdowns, finishing as the WR1 overall on Sunday (29.8 fantasy points). He ran the second-most routes on the team (32), behind Tetairoa McMillan (36), and averaged 13.8 air yards per target and 4.31 yards per route run. He made a very strong opening argument to be a 1B to McMillan's 1A this season. And while all of Carolina's numbers were inflated by this barn-burner of a game with Chicago , Coker had flashed late last year and looks like a legitimate third-year breakout candidate. He'll be among the most-added players on waivers this week (despite starting at 61%) and should be at least a FLEX consideration until further notice.

Elsewhere in this crazy Bears-Panthers game, Chuba Hubbard outsnapped Jonathon Brooks 41-to-13 and outcarried him 10-to-4. And while Brooks broke off a 48-yard reception, he was pretty silent as a rusher. Meanwhile, Hubbard racked up 49 yards on his 10 carries and scored from two yards out on the ground and four yards out through the air. Again, take it with a Chicago grain of salt. But at least for now, Hubbard is the lead back in Carolina and a borderline RB2 for fantasy.

This was somewhat predictable given how the Bills defense played the run last season (terribly), but David Montgomery's three touchdowns on Sunday were pretty encouraging. He only averaged 3.0 yards per carry on 20 totes and added 19 yards on three catches, but Montgomery scored rushing TDs from the goal line and the 18-yard line, and a receiving TD from the seven-yard line as well. If Houston is going to put him in position to score that often — and feed him more than 20 opportunities a game — Montgomery doesn't need to be that efficient to be effective for fantasy. He gets the Bengals next week as well, so expect another RB1-level outing from the artist formerly known as "Knuckles" (unless we're still calling him that).

I promise, I was totally and completely normal about Parker Washington scoring the first touchdown of the Jaguars' 2026 season ... and ultimately putting up 16.8 fantasy points in the first half before essentially taking the rest of the game off in a blowout win. That's right, Washington logged all of his five catches for 83 yards by halftime, and then did not see a target the rest of the day. Jacksonville 's not going to be up 24-0 after two quarters against most opponents — this was the Cleveland Browns after all — so we should get four quarters from Washington moving forward. He's a legitimate WR2 in fantasy (if not better).

Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence has not just Washington, but also a resurgent Brian Thomas Jr. , effective Jakobi Meyers , touchdown-scoring Brenton Strange and productive Bhayshul Tuten to throw to this season. He picked up right where he left off at the end of last season — scorching the league. Lawrence threw four touchdowns and posted a 150.6 passer rating ... and those four scores came on the team's first six drives before the aforementioned second-half coasting. At this rate, Lawrence could very well belong in the elite tier of fantasy QBs with Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson (and maybe Caleb Williams and Jaxson Dart , based on what we saw on Sunday).

Had Dallas Goedert posted a decent day against the Commanders, I might have largely chalked it up to the Washington defense — which was, and clearly still is, terrible against tight ends. But the Eagles tight end was dominant , snagging a team-high four catches for a team-high 77 yards (on five targets) and scoring two touchdowns, including a 43-yarder late in the fourth quarter that essentially sealed the game for Philly. Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith were both good in their roles as well, but with A.J. Brown gone, Goedert looks like he's a focal point of this offense and probably the top red-zone threat (at least from outside the two-yard line). He was a fringe TE1 entering the year but could quickly cement himself near or inside the upper-tier at the position.

Speaking of tight ends taking their place in the elite ranks ... hello, Isaiah Likely. After being stuck behind Mark Andrews for years in Baltimore — and often flashing when given the chance — Likely followed John Harbaugh to New York. And boy did it work out (through one week). Likely was Jaxson Dart's best receiver, snagging all eight of his targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns, and making several critical plays in the eventual 28-20 win over the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. He looked every bit the part of a true TE1 for both Big Blue and for fantasy. I'm not hesitating to put him right in the conversation with Colston Loveland (who we'll get to later), Tyler Warren and Tucker Kraft among the best tight ends not named Trey McBride (or Brock Bowers when healthy). It might sound like an overreaction, but what we saw on Sunday night makes too much sense to ignore. Likely to the moon.

Josh Allen's newest toy, DJ Moore, had an excellent first game with the Bills, catching five passes for 100 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. But even counting the 43-yard bomb that DJM caught for his score, this stat line doesn't tell the full story. Moore also drew an egregious pass interference penalty on a similar downfield pass earlier in the game, which would have resulted in a 47-yard touchdown without the penalty, and instead set up an Allen rushing TD from the one-yard line. Moore ran the most routes on the team and saw 19.4 air yards per target, ultimately accounting for 44% of the Bills' team air yards on the day. Also armed with Khalil Shakir underneath and Dalton Kincaid over the middle — not to mention James Cook II in the ground game — Allen and the Bills offense are poised for a best-ever type of season in 2026. It looks like Moore will thrive at the helm of the passing attack and is a strong WR2 with WR1 upside.

This is hard for me to admit as a long-time Christian Watson denier — and it was probably my worst "fade" of all-time — but the Packers wideout looked dominant on Sunday against what was one of the toughest defenses against wide receivers last year. He started things off with an 81-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the first quarter and proceeded to rack up 147 yards on six catches, with another TD from the two-yard line at the end of the first half. Watson currently sits just behind Coker for the highest fantasy score at the position (29.7 points). But most importantly, he saw eight targets. Watson had only seen eight or more targets five times prior in his career, and only caught six or more passes twice (both more than two years ago). He appears to be the true WR1 in Green Bay , and combining his efficiency with WR1 volume is a terrifying prospect. There's still a part of me that fears this receiving corps will be unpredictable week-to-week and Watson could be an afterthought next Sunday ... but that part is fading quickly.

We knew the Dolphins offense was going to be bad in 2026, and that De'Von Achane was a riskier early fantasy pick as a result. But Achane's unmatched big-play threat and elite receiving upside theoretically mitigated that risk. Welp. In a game Miami trailed throughout, against the Raiders no less, Achane had four receptions for 30 yards, which was nowhere near enough to offset just 36 rushing yards on 11 carries. Moreover, Miami did not have a single drive that finished inside the Raiders' 10-yard line ... and their only touchdown was a 13-yard rush vultured by Malik Willis . Achane will undoubtedly have some big games — perhaps even more often than not — but the floor being single-digit fantasy points in one of the few games all season the Dolphins weren't massive underdogs ... is discouraging.

Drake London/Kyle Pitts Sr., WR/TE, Falcons

There was some hope entering Week 1 that Cooper Rush might be a viable enough backup to support the top receiving options in Atlanta after Tua Tagovailoa 's late injury scratch (and Michael Penix Jr . already out). Not so much. Rush completed just 12 passes against the Steelers ... and eight of those completions went to Bijan Robinson . No, I'm not joking. London and Pitts combined for two catches on five targets for 29 yards (and all the catches and yards were London's). We'll see how the quarterback situation shakes out next week and beyond — and both these players are too talented to be goose-egged or near goose-egged all year — but it's certainly not an encouraging start for players many had near the top of their positions in the preseason rankings.

The good news is that this "fade" from my weekly column sort of balances out the Watson one ... I think? The bad news is that Terry McLaurin might be very hard to trust in fantasy this season. Washington's former WR1 — and yes, I mean that — saw just four targets and caught two for 14 yards. We were looking at a zero in his fantasy box score for the vast majority of the game, and it seemed extremely clear that Jayden Daniels and Co. preferred Stefon Diggs (who drew nine targets). Also, rookie Antonio Williams surged late in the game and might lay claim to a bigger piece of the pie moving forward. It might sound hyperbolically doom-and-gloom, but I was already very out on McLaurin this year and Week 1 was a near "nail-in-the-coffin." He is no longer the clear No. 1 in the DMV, and I do not foresee a major bounce-back in 2026 after a very disappointing 2025. I'd honestly look to trade McLaurin to an optimistic buyer ASAP ... and might even consider Coker as the return.

To put it unkindly, the Cleveland Browns are very, very bad, and that's very, very bad news for Quinshon Judkins. He was outrushed by Deshaun Watson on Sunday (on six fewer carries), finishing with just 33 yards on 12 totes (2.8 per carry) and adding two catches for 17 yards. The Browns didn't get into the red zone until late in the third quarter, and that drive ended in a field goal ... and was their only red-zone drive ending in points all day. And mind you, this dud of an opener for Judkins came with Dylan Sampson (knee) out for essentially the entire game. Working off Sunday's tape, it's hard to imagine a scenario where the Browns put together an effective offense at any point this season, which means Judkins will be incredibly hit-or-miss, based on big plays or occasional touchdowns. He was drafted as an RB2, but is already slipping into RB3 territory after that ineffective an opener.

If you told me entering Week 1 that Colston Loveland would play the entire game, and that the Bears would score 59 points, but that the second-year tight end would finish with zero, zilch, nada ... I would have chuckled and checked your temperature. Unfortunately, that's exactly what happened. It was borderline inexplicable, especially considering Loveland ran the most routes on the team (32) and Cole Kmet had two catches for 35 yards and a touchdown. Honestly, I expect a significant rebound from Loveland moving forward — he's too talented, and Kalif Raymond is unlikely to see nine targets again — but we should not see goose eggs in 59-burgers from our elite fantasy tight ends. Loveland is on "Concern Watch" for the next couple weeks.

articles.title: Celtic captain Callum McGregor hits out at 'team of individuals' after Old Firm League Cup defeat to Rangers
articles.summary: Rangers beat Celtic 3-0 at Ibrox to progress to the League Cup semi-finals; the Hoops host Ferencvaros in the Europa League before hosting Rangers in the Premiership; watch the first Old Firm league game of the season this Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Captain Callum McGregor was scathing in his assessment of Celtic's League Cup defeat to Rangers.

The Hoops travelled to Ibrox for a quarter-final tie against their Old Firm rivals unbeaten in seven domestic games this season.

And McGregor offered no excuses for the 3-0 defeat: "It wasn't us. The difference between the two sides was you saw a team and then you saw a team of individuals as well.

"Rangers were a team and you could see that.

"We looked like a team of individuals who like to do our own thing and play when we got the ball, not necessarily run when you don't have the ball when that's the thing you can't do when you come here.

"You can't defend with six players, it's impossible."

The cup exit comes after Celtic's Champions League qualifying defeat by Austrian side LASK, where they surrendered a 4-0 aggregate lead to be beaten 5-4.

They host Hungarian side Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday before Rangers travel to Celtic Park in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

"We've put ourselves under pressure, we need to respond on Thursday and then we need to respond on Sunday but we very quickly need to get to the level," McGregor added.

"But trying to get the message to everyone that we have to be the team that we want to be.

"We need to find a way to do that quickly because we lost a big game against LASK and we lost another big game on Sunday and it's not acceptable.

"There'll be other big games throughout the season and eventually you have to win one if you want to be considered a good team.

"If we want to be a good Celtic team then we'll have to win the big games. One thing we've always done is win big games and turned up when it mattered.

"So far this season we've been bitty in games and we need to fix it."

With the memories of Austria still fresh in his mind, McGregor feared the defeat could have been even more damaging.

He said: "Yeah, you don't want fours and fives for sure.

"As soon as the goals go in, then I'm saying to Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales, no more goals.

"We need to just tighten this up. Of course we always want to get back in the game, we always want to be a team that, even at 3-0 down you still want to have a chance.

"But you have to understand the circumstances as well, well beaten at 3-0 with good goals against you, but if it starts to run at fours and fives then you're talking about a different ball game."

articles.title: Excepcional campaña de Lamine para el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: A falta de dos semanas para el cierre de las votaciones para el trofeo, se sale en el césped
articles.summary: A falta de dos semanas para el cierre de las votaciones para el trofeo, se sale en el césped
articles.body: Lamine Yamal no va a suplicar para ganar el Balón de Oro, lo comentó en rueda de prensa hace unos días. Pero cree que se lo merece, como dijo entonces en esa misma comparecencia y ha repetido en más ocasiones. La competencia por el valorado trofeo es dura, pero el canterano culé está exhibiendo su firme candidatura con su rendimiento en el campo. El Barça está en plena campaña para que lo conquiste, pero el extremo no necesita ayuda: su productividad en los últimos partidos le avalan, y confirman, como uno de los mejores jugadores del mundo. Dentro de dos semanas, el día 28, concluye el plazo para que los 100 profesionales del periodismo de los países del ránking FIFA voten para el Balón de Oro, que en esta edición se entrega en el teatro London Palladium el 26 de octubre. Entre los 30 finalistas destacan, además de Lamine, Kane, Jude Bellingham, Mbappé, Dembélé, Haaland, Messi, Pau Cubarsí, Marc Cucurella, Rodri Hernández, Fabián Ruiz, Bruno Fernandes, Ferran Torres... "Mbappé y yo somos los dos mejores, pero creo que el Balón de Oro me lo merecería yo", sentenció el canterano culé en una entrevista en 'Universo Valdano' de Movistar Plus. La pugna es, sin duda, dura, pero su rendimiento en este arranque de curso y especialmente en los cuatro últimos encuentros puede de resultarle de gran ayuda. El internacional suma siete goles y dos asistencias en los seis partidos disputados: cinco de LaLiga y uno de la Champions League. Pero en los cuatro más recientes, jugados contra Rayo, Valencia y Levante en el torneo nacional y Feyenoord en el europeo, ha visto puerta, firmando un doblete en los tres cruces de nivel estatal. Lamine, gracias a estos números, suma seis tantos en LaLiga y es uno de los futbolistas que lideran el Pichichi, junto a Camello, Mbappé y Raphinha. Así las cosas, el joven extremo, de 19 años, está haciendo méritos en el campo para conquistar el Balón de Oro. No requiere una campaña, aunque desde el Barcelona impulsan su candidatura. "Espero que se haga justicia y se lo den a Lamine", comentó hace unas horas el vicepresidente Rafa Yuste. "Es uno de los grandes favoritos y me encantaría que lo ganara. Está espectacular. Tiene una calidad excepcional. Es un genio", aseveró, por su parte, Laporta hace unos días Sus compañeros de vestuario también han defendido estas jornadas atrás que debería ser distinguido con el preciado galardón. Los parámetros que rigen las votaciones al trofeo son: actuaciones individuales con un carácter decisivo e impresionante; resultados colectivos y los títulos conseguidos con club y selección; y la clase y el juego limpio. Lamine, sin duda, es uno de los favoritos por su cómputo general en los tres criterios, pero aún le restan dos semanas para lograr auparse al primer puesto.

articles.title: Kiko Casilla: "Nadie puede criticar cómo está rindiendo Courtois"
articles.standfirst: El exguardameta del Real Madrid y del Elche analiza en Marcador el momento de ambos equipos, defiende el rendimiento de Courtois y destaca el récord de Soria con el Getafe
articles.summary: El exguardameta del Real Madrid y del Elche analiza en Marcador el momento de ambos equipos, defiende el rendimiento de Courtois y destaca el récord de Soria con el Getafe
articles.body: Kiko Casilla pasó por los micrófonos de Marcador, con Israel Herraiz, para analizar el duelo entre el Elche y el Real Madrid. El exguardameta, que conoce bien ambas camisetas, recordó la exigencia que supone defender la portería del conjunto blanco: "Desde los 14 años he tenido la suerte de saber lo que pesa", explicó. Una presión que, según reconoce, se hace todavía mayor cuando llega el momento de jugar en el primer equipo y, especialmente, en el Santiago Bernabéu: "Cuando te la pones en el primer equipo y sobre todo en el Bernabéu, es muy exigente, se nota". Uno de los nombres propios de la conversación fue Thibaut Courtois. Casilla se mostró contundente al valorar el rendimiento del belga y rechazó las críticas que apuntan a un descenso de nivel por el paso de los años: "Nadie puede criticar cómo está rindiendo", afirmó. Para el exmadridista, la regularidad del portero es diferencial: "Es un tío que está dando muchos puntos, que está dando mucha tranquilidad". Además, destacó que tanto Courtois como Lunin están ofreciendo garantías bajo palos. Sobre el Elche, Casilla entiende que el cambio de entrenador después de la etapa de Eder Sarabia puede explicar parte de las dificultades del inicio: "Cambiar ese estilo de entrenador va a costar y más en la élite, en Primera División", señaló. El exguardameta considera que el equipo necesita tiempo y, sobre todo, una victoria que permita recuperar la confianza: "Hay que empezar a ganar un partido y todo se verá diferente". También defendió el potencial de la plantilla y pidió tranquilidad para el nuevo proyecto. Casilla también salió en defensa de Matías Dituro después de su error ante el Racing de Santander. El exguardameta destacó que el argentino dio la cara desde el primer momento y que ahora debe centrarse en el trabajo: "Tiene ya unos años de veteranía que creo que se le puede ir bien para quitarse un poco el foco de ese error y seguir trabajando", explicó. Además, rechazó la idea de sustituir inmediatamente a un portero tras cometer un fallo grave y puso como ejemplo el caso de Antonín Kinský, sustituido después de dos errores ante el Atlético de Madrid. Para Casilla, el guardameta del Elche tiene la personalidad y la experiencia necesarias para recuperse. La conversación también sirvió para recordar la importancia de la continuidad y del trabajo diario en una posición tan particular como la portería. Casilla explicó que, cuando un guardameta no juega habitualmente, debe estar preparado para aprovechar su oportunidad sin querer demostrar más de la cuenta: "Que te vean tranquilo, sobre todo. Saber también tu rol dentro del equipo y, sobre todo, ayudar", resumió. El exmadridista habló además de su experiencia en el Real Madrid y de la exigencia del Bernabéu, donde incluso una ventaja de 2-0 puede venir acompañada del famoso ‘rum-rum’ de la grada: "Hay que saber llevarlo y yo creo que cualquier jugador que está en el Real Madrid sabe de esa exigencia y está acostumbrado", explicó. Casilla también tuvo palabras para David Soria, con quien coincidió en el Getafe, después de que el guardameta haya alcanzado las 193 titularidades consecutivas. "Una locura. Me alegro mucho. Primero que es un tipo espectacular, ya como persona, pero como portero también lo ha demostrado año a año", aseguró. El exguardameta quiso felicitarle por el récord y deseó "todo lo mejor" tanto a Soria como a Bordalás y al Getafe en su aventura europea.

articles.title: Texas' Sarkisian Defends Ohio State, Buckeyes Shouldn't Be 'Punished' by CFP Committee for Loss
articles.summary: Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian doesn't believe the College Football Playoff Committee should punish Ohio State for Saturday's 24-23 loss in Austin.
articles.body:
Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian doesn't believe the College Football Playoff Committee should punish Ohio State for Saturday's 24-23 loss in Austin.

"I hope Ohio State does not get punished for that game Saturday night," he told reporters Monday. "They played a heck of a game. I mean, it's 24-23. They lose scoring with 25 seconds to go in the game. That I hope if they end up being a 9–3 team, the Committee can appreciate the fact that they came to Austin, Texas, in September when it was 100 degrees and played us in that environment and played a heck of a game. And so they should not be punished. Quite frankly, Ohio State should be rewarded for playing in this game against us."

While Sarkisian's comments were gracious, they may have also been a bit pointed after Texas lost 14-7 in Columbus last season, ultimately finished the regular season 9-3 and were ranked No. 13, leaving them out of the College Football Playoff.

Granted, it was a bad loss against a Florida team (which ultimately finished 4-8) that likely soured Texas in the eyes of voters. Plus, a pair of two-loss teams ranked above Texas—Notre Dame and BYU—also failed to get in the CFP. While three-loss Alabama did get in, the third loss came in the SEC Championship Game.

As for Ohio State, the Associated Press voters didn't dock the Buckeyes too harshly for Saturday's loss, dropping them from No. 1 to No. 6. Texas, meanwhile, jumped from No. 4 to No. 1.

Ohio State has to run a Big Ten gauntlet this season, however, with matchups against Iowa, Indiana, USC, Oregon and Michigan yet to come. All five teams are currently ranked in the top 25.

The Buckeyes don't have much margin for error left, in other words, though they are also loaded with talent. But Sarkisian doesn't believe a close loss in Austin should be held against them.
